# uom 0.38.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/uom/0.38.0

# uom

Units of measurement is a crate that does automatic type-safe zero-cost
[dimensional analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimensional_analysis). You can create your own systems or use the pre-built
[International System of Units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html) (SI) which is based on the
[International System of Quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.6.html) (ISQ) and includes numerous [quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.1.html)
(length, mass, time, ...) with conversion factors for even more numerous
[measurement units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.9.html) (meter, kilometer, foot, mile, ...). No more crashing your
[climate orbiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_Climate_Orbiter)!

## Usage

`uom` requires `rustc` 1.68.0 or later. Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "0.38.0"
```
and this to your crate root:

```
extern crate uom;
```
The simple example below shows how to use quantities and units as well as how `uom` stops invalid
operations:

```
extern crate uom;
use *;
use kilometer;
use second;
```
See the [examples](https://docs.rs/examples) directory for more advanced usage:

- [si.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/si.rs)-- Shows how to use the pre-built SI system.
- [base.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/base.rs)-- Shows how to create a set of- `Quantity`type aliases for a different set of base units. See the- [Design](https://docs.rs#design)section for implications of choosing different base units.
- [mks.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/mks.rs)-- Shows how to create a custom system of quantities.
- [unit.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/unit.rs)-- Shows how to add new units to existing quantities in the pre-build SI system.

## Features

`uom` has multiple `Cargo` features for controlling available underlying storage types, the
inclusion of the pre-built [International System of Units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html) (SI), support for [Serde](https://serde.rs/),
and `no_std` functionality. The features are described below. `f32`, `f64`, `std`, and `si` are
enabled by default. Features can be cherry-picked by using the `--no-default-features` and
`--features "..."` flags when compiling `uom` or specifying features in Cargo.toml:

```
[]
 = {
    version = "0.38.0",
     = false,
     = [
        "autoconvert", # automatic base unit conversion.
        "usize", "u8", "u16", "u32", "u64", "u128", # Unsigned integer storage types.
        "isize", "i8", "i16", "i32", "i64", "i128", # Signed integer storage types.
        "bigint", "biguint", # Arbitrary width integer storage types.
        "rational", "rational32", "rational64", "bigrational", # Integer ratio storage types.
        "complex32", "complex64", # Complex floating point storage types.
        "f32", "f64", # Floating point storage types.
        "si", "std", # Built-in SI system and std library support.
        "serde", # Serde support.
    ]
}
```
- `autoconvert`-- Feature to enable automatic conversion between base units in binary operators. Disabling the feature only allows for quantities with the same base units to directly interact. The feature exists to account for compiler limitations where zero-cost code is not generated for non-floating point underlying storage types.
- `usize`,- `u8`,- `u16`,- `u32`,- `u64`,- `u128`,- `isize`,- `i8`,- `i16`,- `i32`,- `i64`,- `i128`,- `bigint`,- `biguint`,- `rational`,- `rational32`,- `rational64`,- `bigrational`,- `complex32`,- `complex64`,- `f32`,- `f64`-- Features to enable underlying storage types. At least one of these features must be enabled.- `f32`and- `f64`are enabled by default. See the- [Design](https://docs.rs#design)section for implications of choosing different underlying storage types.
- `si`-- Feature to include the pre-built- [International System of Units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html)(SI). Enabled by default.
- `std`-- Feature to compile with standard library support. Disabling this feature compiles- `uom`with- `no_std`. Enabled by default.
- `serde`-- Feature to enable support for serialization and deserialization of quantities with the- [Serde](https://serde.rs/)crate. Disabled by default. Replaces the deprecated- `use_serde`feature, which will be removed in a future- `uom`release (v0.37.0 or later).

## Design

Rather than working with [measurement units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.9.html) (meter,
kilometer, foot, mile, ...) `uom` works with [quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.1.html)
(length, mass, time, ...). This simplifies usage because units are only involved at interface
boundaries: the rest of your code only needs to be concerned about the quantities involved. This
also makes operations on quantities (+, -, *, /, ...) have zero runtime cost over using the raw
storage type (e.g. `f32`).

`uom` normalizes values to the [base unit](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.10.html) for the quantity.
Alternative base units can be used by executing the macro defined for the system of quantities
(`ISQ!` for the SI). `uom` supports `usize`, `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `u128`, `isize`, `i8`,
`i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `i128`, `bigint`, `biguint`, `rational`, `rational32`, `rational64`,
`bigrational`, `complex32`, `complex64`, `f32`, and `f64` as the underlying storage type.

A consequence of normalizing values to the base unit is that some values may not be able to be
represented or can't be precisely represented for floating point and rational underlying storage
types. For example if the base unit of `length` is `meter` and the underlying storage type is `i32`
then values like `1 centimeter` or `1.1 meter` cannot be represented. `1 centimeter` is normalized
to `0.01 meter` which can't be stored in an `i32`. `uom` only allows units to be used safely. Users
of this library will still need to be aware of implementation details of the underlying storage type
including limits and precision.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome from everyone. Submit a pull request, an issue, or just add comments to an
existing item. The [International Bureau of Weights and Measures](https://www.bipm.org/en/about-us/) is an international
standards organization that publishes the [SI Brochure](https://www.bipm.org/en/publications/si-brochure/). This document defines the [SI](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html)
and can be used as a comprehensive reference for changes to `uom`. Conversion factors for non-SI
units can be found in NIST [Special Publication 811](https://www.nist.gov/pml/special-publication-811/nist-guide-si-appendix-b-conversion-factors/nist-guide-si-appendix-b9).

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in the work by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as below, without any additional terms or conditions.

Licensed under either of

- Apache License, Version 2.0, ([LICENSE-APACHE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-APACHE)or[https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0))

at your option.

# uom - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/uom/0.38.0/target-redirect/uom/

## Expand description

Units of measurement is a crate that does automatic type-safe zero-cost
[dimensional analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimensional_analysis). You can create your own systems or use the pre-built
[International System of Units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html) (SI) which is based on the
[International System of Quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.6.html) (ISQ) and includes numerous [quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.1.html)
(length, mass, time, …) with conversion factors for even more numerous
[measurement units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.9.html) (meter, kilometer, foot, mile, …). No more crashing your
[climate orbiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_Climate_Orbiter)!

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

`uom` requires `rustc` 1.68.0 or later. Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies]
uom = "0.38.0"
```
and this to your crate root:

`extern crate uom;`The simple example below shows how to use quantities and units as well as how `uom` stops
invalid operations:

```
extern crate uom;
use uom::si::f32::*;
use uom::si::length::kilometer;
use uom::si::time::second;
fn main() {
   let length = Length::new::<kilometer>(5.0);
   let time = Time::new::<second>(15.0);
   let velocity/*: Velocity*/ = length / time;
   let _acceleration = calc_acceleration(velocity, time);
   //let error = length + time; // error[E0308]: mismatched types
   // Get a quantity value in a specific unit.
   let time_in_nano_seconds = time.get::<uom::si::time::nanosecond>();
}
fn calc_acceleration(velocity: Velocity, time: Time) -> Acceleration {
   velocity / time
}
```
See examples provided with the source for more advanced usage including how to create `Quantity`
type aliases for a different set of base units and how to create an entirely new system of
quantities.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [ISQ](https://docs.rs/macro.ISQ.html)
- Macro to implement `Quantity`[system of units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.13.html)and value storage type.
- [impl_](https://docs.rs/macro.impl_from.html)- from
- `impl_from`generates generic inter-Kind implementations of- `From`.
- [prefix](https://docs.rs/macro.prefix.html)
- Macro to implement the [SI](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html)prefixes for[multiples of units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.17.html),[submultiples of units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.18.html)and[binary multiples of units](https://www.iec.ch/si/binary.htm).
- [quantity](https://docs.rs/macro.quantity.html)
- Macro to implement a [quantity](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.1.html)and associated[measurement units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.9.html). Note that this macro must be executed in direct submodules of the module where the`system!`
- [storage_](https://docs.rs/macro.storage_types.html)- types
- Macro to duplicate code on a per-storage type basis. The given code is duplicated in new
modules named for each storage type. A type alias, `V`, is generated that code can use for the type.
- [system](https://docs.rs/macro.system.html)
- Macro to implement a [system of quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.3.html).
- [unit](https://docs.rs/macro.unit.html)
- Macro to implement a set of [measurement units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.9.html). Note that units manually defined using this macro will not be included in the quantity unit enum or associated functions, or in the`FromStr`implementation. Using this macro will create submodules for the underlying storage types that are enabled (e.g.`mod f32`).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Constant](https://docs.rs/enum.ConstantOp.html)- Op
- Operations performed on the constant portion of the [conversion factor](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.24.html). Used to help guide optimizations when floating point underlying storage types are used.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

# uom - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uom/0.38.0/uom/index.html

## Expand description

Units of measurement is a crate that does automatic type-safe zero-cost
[dimensional analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimensional_analysis). You can create your own systems or use the pre-built
[International System of Units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html) (SI) which is based on the
[International System of Quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.6.html) (ISQ) and includes numerous [quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.1.html)
(length, mass, time, …) with conversion factors for even more numerous
[measurement units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.9.html) (meter, kilometer, foot, mile, …). No more crashing your
[climate orbiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_Climate_Orbiter)!

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

`uom` requires `rustc` 1.68.0 or later. Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies]
uom = "0.38.0"
```
and this to your crate root:

`extern crate uom;`The simple example below shows how to use quantities and units as well as how `uom` stops
invalid operations:

```
extern crate uom;
use uom::si::f32::*;
use uom::si::length::kilometer;
use uom::si::time::second;
fn main() {
   let length = Length::new::<kilometer>(5.0);
   let time = Time::new::<second>(15.0);
   let velocity/*: Velocity*/ = length / time;
   let _acceleration = calc_acceleration(velocity, time);
   //let error = length + time; // error[E0308]: mismatched types
   // Get a quantity value in a specific unit.
   let time_in_nano_seconds = time.get::<uom::si::time::nanosecond>();
}
fn calc_acceleration(velocity: Velocity, time: Time) -> Acceleration {
   velocity / time
}
```
See examples provided with the source for more advanced usage including how to create `Quantity`
type aliases for a different set of base units and how to create an entirely new system of
quantities.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

`uom` has multiple `Cargo` features for controlling available underlying storage types, the
inclusion of the pre-built [International System of Units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html) (SI), support for
[Serde](https://serde.rs/), and `no_std` functionality. The features are described below. `f32`, `f64`,
`std`, and `si` are enabled by default. Features can be cherry-picked by using the
`--no-default-features` and `--features "..."` flags when compiling `uom` or specifying
features in Cargo.toml:

```
[dependencies]
uom = {
    version = "0.38.0",
    default-features = false,
    features = [
        "autoconvert", # automatic base unit conversion.
        "usize", "u8", "u16", "u32", "u64", "u128", # Unsigned integer storage types.
        "isize", "i8", "i16", "i32", "i64", "i128", # Signed integer storage types.
        "bigint", "biguint", # Arbitrary width integer storage types.
        "rational", "rational32", "rational64", "bigrational", # Integer ratio storage types.
        "complex32", "complex64", # Complex floating point storage types.
        "f32", "f64", # Floating point storage types.
        "si", "std", # Built-in SI system and std library support.
        "serde", # Serde support.
    ]
}
```
- `autoconvert`– Feature to enable automatic conversion between base units in binary operators. Disabling the feature only allows for quantities with the same base units to directly interact. The feature exists to account for compiler limitations where zero-cost code is not generated for non-floating point underlying storage types.
- `usize`,- `u8`,- `u16`,- `u32`,- `u64`,- `u128`,- `isize`,- `i8`,- `i16`,- `i32`,- `i64`,- `i128`,- `bigint`,- `biguint`,- `rational`,- `rational32`,- `rational64`,- `bigrational`,- `complex32`,- `complex64`,- `f32`,- `f64`– Features to enable underlying storage types. At least one of these features must be enabled.- `f32`and- `f64`are enabled by default. See the- [Design](https://docs.rs#design)section for implications of choosing different underlying storage types.
- `si`– Feature to include the pre-built- [International System of Units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html)(SI). Enabled by default.
- `std`– Feature to compile with standard library support. Disabling this feature compiles- `uom`with- `no_std`. Enabled by default.
- `serde`– Feature to enable support for serialization and deserialization of quantities with the- [Serde](https://serde.rs/)crate. Disabled by default.

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

Rather than working with [measurement units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.9.html) (meter,
kilometer, foot, mile, …) `uom` works with [quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.1.html)
(length, mass, time, …). This simplifies usage because units are only involved at interface
boundaries: the rest of your code only needs to be concerned about the quantities involved.
This also makes operations on quantities (+, -, *, /, …) have zero runtime cost over using
the raw storage type (e.g. `f32`).

`uom` normalizes values to the [base unit](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.10.html) for the
quantity. Alternative base units can be used by executing the macro defined for the system of
quantities (`ISQ!` for the SI). `uom` supports `usize`, `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `u128`,
`isize`, `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `i128`, `bigint`, `biguint`, `rational`, `rational32`,
`rational64`, `bigrational`, `complex32`, `complex64`, `f32`, and `f64` as the underlying
storage type.

A consequence of normalizing values to the base unit is that some values may not be able to be
represented or can’t be precisely represented for floating point and rational underlying
storage types. For example if the base unit of `length` is `meter` and the underlying storage
type is `i32` then values like `1 centimeter` or `1.1 meter` cannot be represented. `1 centimeter` is normalized to `0.01 meter` which can’t be stored in an `i32`. `uom` only allows
units to be used safely. Users of this library will still need to be aware of implementation
details of the underlying storage type including limits and precision.

[§](https://docs.rs#contributing)Contributing

Contributions are welcome from everyone. Submit a pull request, an issue, or just add comments
to an existing item. The [International Bureau of Weights and Measures](https://www.bipm.org/en/about-us/) is an
international standards organization that publishes the [SI Brochure](https://www.bipm.org/en/publications/si-brochure/). This document
defines the [SI](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html) and can be used as a comprehensive reference for changes to `uom`. Conversion
factors for non-SI units can be found in NIST [Special Publication 811](https://www.nist.gov/pml/special-publication-811/nist-guide-si-appendix-b-conversion-factors/nist-guide-si-appendix-b9).

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in the work by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as below, without any additional terms or conditions.

- [storage_](https://docs.rs/macro.storage_types.html)- types
- Macro to duplicate code on a per-storage type basis. The given code is duplicated in new
modules named for each storage type. A type alias, `V`, is generated that code can use for the type.
- [system](https://docs.rs/macro.system.html)
- Macro to implement a [system of quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.3.html).
- [unit](https://docs.rs/macro.unit.html)
- Macro to implement a set of [measurement units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.9.html). Note that units manually defined using this macro will not be included in the quantity unit enum or associated functions, or in the`FromStr`implementation. Using this macro will create submodules for the underlying storage types that are enabled (e.g.`mod f32`).

# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/uom/0.38.0/src/uom/lib.rs.html

# uom/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Units of measurement is a crate that does automatic type-safe zero-cost
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//! [dimensional analysis][analysis]. You can create your own systems or use the pre-built
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! [International System of Units][si] (SI) which is based on the
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! [International System of Quantities][isq] (ISQ) and includes numerous [quantities][quantity]
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! (length, mass, time, ...) with conversion factors for even more numerous
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! [measurement units][measurement] (meter, kilometer, foot, mile, ...). No more crashing your
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! [climate orbiter][orbiter]!
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//!
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! [analysis]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimensional_analysis
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! [si]: https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! [isq]: https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.6.html
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! [quantity]: https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.1.html
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! [measurement]: https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.9.html
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! [orbiter]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_Climate_Orbiter
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//!
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! ## Usage
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! `uom` requires `rustc` 1.68.0 or later. Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//!
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! ```toml
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! [dependencies]
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! uom = "0.38.0"
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! ```
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! and this to your crate root:
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//!
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! ```rust
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! extern crate uom;
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! ```
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//!
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! The simple example below shows how to use quantities and units as well as how `uom` stops
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! invalid operations:
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//!
[33](https://docs.rs#33)#![cfg_attr(all(feature = "si", feature = "f32"), doc = " ```rust")]
[34](https://docs.rs#34)#![cfg_attr(not(all(feature = "si", feature = "f32")), doc = " ```rust,ignore")]
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! extern crate uom;
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! use uom::si::f32::*;
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! use uom::si::length::kilometer;
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! use uom::si::time::second;
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//!
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! fn main() {
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//!     let length = Length::new::<kilometer>(5.0);
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//!     let time = Time::new::<second>(15.0);
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//!     let velocity/*: Velocity*/ = length / time;
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//!     let _acceleration = calc_acceleration(velocity, time);
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!     //let error = length + time; // error[E0308]: mismatched types
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//!
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//!     // Get a quantity value in a specific unit.
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//!     let time_in_nano_seconds = time.get::<uom::si::time::nanosecond>();
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! }
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//!
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! fn calc_acceleration(velocity: Velocity, time: Time) -> Acceleration {
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!     velocity / time
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! }
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//! ```
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//!
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//! See examples provided with the source for more advanced usage including how to create `Quantity`
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! type aliases for a different set of base units and how to create an entirely new system of
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! quantities.
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//!
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//! ## Features
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! `uom` has multiple `Cargo` features for controlling available underlying storage types, the
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//! inclusion of the pre-built [International System of Units][si] (SI), support for
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//! [Serde][serde], and `no_std` functionality. The features are described below. `f32`, `f64`,
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//! `std`, and `si` are enabled by default. Features can be cherry-picked by using the
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! `--no-default-features` and `--features "..."` flags when compiling `uom` or specifying
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! features in Cargo.toml:
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//!
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! ```toml
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! [dependencies]
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//! uom = {
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//!     version = "0.38.0",
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//!     default-features = false,
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//!     features = [
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//!         "autoconvert", # automatic base unit conversion.
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//!         "usize", "u8", "u16", "u32", "u64", "u128", # Unsigned integer storage types.
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//!         "isize", "i8", "i16", "i32", "i64", "i128", # Signed integer storage types.
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//!         "bigint", "biguint", # Arbitrary width integer storage types.
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//!         "rational", "rational32", "rational64", "bigrational", # Integer ratio storage types.
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//!         "complex32", "complex64", # Complex floating point storage types.
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//!         "f32", "f64", # Floating point storage types.
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//!         "si", "std", # Built-in SI system and std library support.
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//!         "serde", # Serde support.
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//!     ]
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//! }
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! ```
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//!
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//!  * `autoconvert` -- Feature to enable automatic conversion between base units in binary
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//!    operators. Disabling the feature only allows for quantities with the same base units to
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//!    directly interact. The feature exists to account for compiler limitations where zero-cost
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//!    code is not generated for non-floating point underlying storage types.
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//!  * `usize`, `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `u128`, `isize`, `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `i128`,
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//!    `bigint`, `biguint`, `rational`, `rational32`, `rational64`, `bigrational`, `complex32`,
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//!    `complex64`, `f32`, `f64` -- Features to enable underlying storage types. At least one of
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//!    these features must be enabled. `f32` and `f64` are enabled by default. See the
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//!    [Design](#design) section for implications of choosing different underlying storage types.
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//!  * `si` -- Feature to include the pre-built [International System of Units][si] (SI). Enabled by
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//!    default.
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//!  * `std` -- Feature to compile with standard library support. Disabling this feature compiles
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//!    `uom` with `no_std`. Enabled by default.
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//!  * `serde` -- Feature to enable support for serialization and deserialization of quantities with
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//!    the [Serde][serde] crate. Disabled by default.
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//!
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//! [si]: https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//! [serde]: https://serde.rs/
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//!
[107](https://docs.rs#107)//! ## Design
[108](https://docs.rs#108)//! Rather than working with [measurement units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.9.html) (meter,
[109](https://docs.rs#109)//! kilometer, foot, mile, ...) `uom` works with [quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.1.html)
[110](https://docs.rs#110)//! (length, mass, time, ...). This simplifies usage because units are only involved at interface
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//! boundaries: the rest of your code only needs to be concerned about the quantities involved.
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//! This also makes operations on quantities (+, -, \*, /, ...) have zero runtime cost over using
[113](https://docs.rs#113)//! the raw storage type (e.g. `f32`).
[114](https://docs.rs#114)//!
[115](https://docs.rs#115)//! `uom` normalizes values to the [base unit](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.10.html) for the
[116](https://docs.rs#116)//! quantity. Alternative base units can be used by executing the macro defined for the system of
[117](https://docs.rs#117)//! quantities (`ISQ!` for the SI). `uom` supports `usize`, `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `u128`,
[118](https://docs.rs#118)//! `isize`, `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `i128`, `bigint`, `biguint`, `rational`, `rational32`,
[119](https://docs.rs#119)//! `rational64`, `bigrational`, `complex32`, `complex64`, `f32`, and `f64` as the underlying
[120](https://docs.rs#120)//! storage type.
[121](https://docs.rs#121)//!
[122](https://docs.rs#122)//! A consequence of normalizing values to the base unit is that some values may not be able to be
[123](https://docs.rs#123)//! represented or can't be precisely represented for floating point and rational underlying
[124](https://docs.rs#124)//! storage types. For example if the base unit of `length` is `meter` and the underlying storage
[125](https://docs.rs#125)//! type is `i32` then values like `1 centimeter` or `1.1 meter` cannot be represented. `1
[126](https://docs.rs#126)//! centimeter` is normalized to `0.01 meter` which can't be stored in an `i32`. `uom` only allows
[127](https://docs.rs#127)//! units to be used safely. Users of this library will still need to be aware of implementation
[128](https://docs.rs#128)//! details of the underlying storage type including limits and precision.
[129](https://docs.rs#129)//!
[130](https://docs.rs#130)//! ## Contributing
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//! Contributions are welcome from everyone. Submit a pull request, an issue, or just add comments
[132](https://docs.rs#132)//! to an existing item. The [International Bureau of Weights and Measures][BIPM] is an
[133](https://docs.rs#133)//! international standards organization that publishes the [SI Brochure][brochure]. This document
[134](https://docs.rs#134)//! defines the [SI] and can be used as a comprehensive reference for changes to `uom`. Conversion
[135](https://docs.rs#135)//! factors for non-SI units can be found in NIST [Special Publication 811][nist811].
[136](https://docs.rs#136)//!
[137](https://docs.rs#137)//! Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in
[138](https://docs.rs#138)//! the work by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as below, without
[139](https://docs.rs#139)//! any additional terms or conditions.

[238](https://docs.rs#238)    // Re-export `ops` module along with `typenum::ops` to provide all types in a single mod. This
[239](https://docs.rs#239)    // allows the `system!` macro to reference all operations by the absolute path. Macro paths and
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    // idents can't easily be combined without a `use` statement that pollutes the macro execution
[241](https://docs.rs#241)    // location's namespace.
[242](https://docs.rs#242)    pub mod ops {
[243](https://docs.rs#243)        #[cfg(not(feature = "std"))]
[244](https://docs.rs#244)        pub use core::ops::*;
[245](https://docs.rs#245)        #[cfg(feature = "std")]
[246](https://docs.rs#246)        pub use std::ops::*;
[247](https://docs.rs#247)        pub use typenum::type_operators::*;
[248](https://docs.rs#248)    }
[249](https://docs.rs#249)
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    // Export `panic` module when the `std` feature is not enabled. `RefUnwindSafe` and `UnwindSafe`
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    // traits do not exist in `core` but are conditionally needed in traits defined by `uom` when
[252](https://docs.rs#252)    // `std` is enabled. These definitions work around conditional requirements.
[253](https://docs.rs#253)    #[cfg(not(feature = "std"))]
[254](https://docs.rs#254)    pub mod panic {
[255](https://docs.rs#255)        pub trait RefUnwindSafe {}
[256](https://docs.rs#256)        pub trait UnwindSafe {}
[257](https://docs.rs#257)    }

[374](https://docs.rs#374)/// Operations performed on the constant portion of the [conversion factor][factor]. Used to help
[375](https://docs.rs#375)/// guide optimizations when floating point underlying storage types are used.
[376](https://docs.rs#376)///
[377](https://docs.rs#377)/// For a value, `v: Float`, adding `-0.0` is a no-op while adding `0.0` will change the sign if
[378](https://docs.rs#378)/// `v` is `-0.0`. The opposite is true for subtraction.
[379](https://docs.rs#379)///
[380](https://docs.rs#380)/// ```ignore
[381](https://docs.rs#381)///    v
[382](https://docs.rs#382)///  0.0 + -0.0 =  0.0
[383](https://docs.rs#383)/// -0.0 +  0.0 =  0.0 // v +  0.0 != v
[384](https://docs.rs#384)/// -0.0 + -0.0 = -0.0
[385](https://docs.rs#385)///  0.0 - -0.0 =  0.0
[386](https://docs.rs#386)/// -0.0 -  0.0 =  0.0
[387](https://docs.rs#387)/// -0.0 - -0.0 =  0.0 // v - -0.0 != v
[388](https://docs.rs#388)/// ```
[389](https://docs.rs#389)///
[390](https://docs.rs#390)/// [factor]: https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.24.html
[391](https://docs.rs#391)#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
[392](https://docs.rs#392)pub enum ConstantOp {
[393](https://docs.rs#393)    /// Hint that the constant is being added to a value.
[394](https://docs.rs#394)    Add,
[395](https://docs.rs#395)
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    /// Hint that the constant is being subtracted from a value.
[397](https://docs.rs#397)    Sub,
[398](https://docs.rs#398)}
[399](https://docs.rs#399)
[400](https://docs.rs#400)/// Trait to identify [units][units] which have a [conversion factor][factor].
[401](https://docs.rs#401)///
[402](https://docs.rs#402)/// ## Generic Parameters
[403](https://docs.rs#403)/// * `V`: Underlying storage type trait is implemented for.
[404](https://docs.rs#404)///
[405](https://docs.rs#405)/// [units]: https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.13.html
[406](https://docs.rs#406)/// [factor]: https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.24.html
[407](https://docs.rs#407)pub trait Conversion<V> {
[408](https://docs.rs#408)    /// Conversion factor type specific to the underlying storage type.
[409](https://docs.rs#409)    type T: ConversionFactor<V>;
[410](https://docs.rs#410)
[411](https://docs.rs#411)    /// Coefficient portion of [conversion factor](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.24.html) for
[412](https://docs.rs#412)    /// converting the given unit. To convert to the base unit for the quantity use `(value +
[413](https://docs.rs#413)    /// constant()) * coefficient()`. To convert from the base unit, `(value / coefficient()) -
[414](https://docs.rs#414)    /// constant()` is used. Implementation should return the multiplicative identity
[415](https://docs.rs#415)    /// (`Self::T::one()`) if no coefficient exists.
[416](https://docs.rs#416)    #[must_use = "method returns a new number and does not mutate the original value"]
[417](https://docs.rs#417)    #[inline(always)]
[418](https://docs.rs#418)    fn coefficient() -> Self::T {
[419](https://docs.rs#419)        <Self::T as num::One>::one()
[420](https://docs.rs#420)    }
[421](https://docs.rs#421)
[422](https://docs.rs#422)    /// Constant portion of [conversion factor](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.24.html) for
[423](https://docs.rs#423)    /// converting the given unit. To convert to the base unit for the quantity use `(value +
[424](https://docs.rs#424)    /// constant()) * coefficient()`. To convert from the base unit, `(value / coefficient()) -
[425](https://docs.rs#425)    /// constant()` is used. Implementation should return the additive identity (`Self::T::zero()`)
[426](https://docs.rs#426)    /// if no constant exists. See [`ConstantOp`] documentation for details about parameter use to
[427](https://docs.rs#427)    /// ensure the method optimizes correctly.
[428](https://docs.rs#428)    #[must_use = "method returns a new number and does not mutate the original value"]
[429](https://docs.rs#429)    #[inline(always)]
[430](https://docs.rs#430)    #[allow(unused_variables)]
[431](https://docs.rs#431)    fn constant(op: ConstantOp) -> Self::T {
[432](https://docs.rs#432)        <Self::T as num::Zero>::zero()
[433](https://docs.rs#433)    }
[434](https://docs.rs#434)
[435](https://docs.rs#435)    /// Instance [conversion factor](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.24.html).
[436](https://docs.rs#436)    ///
[437](https://docs.rs#437)    /// Default implementation returns the coefficient: `Self::coefficient()`.
[438](https://docs.rs#438)    #[must_use = "method returns a new number and does not mutate the original value"]
[439](https://docs.rs#439)    #[inline(always)]
[440](https://docs.rs#440)    fn conversion(&self) -> Self::T
[441](https://docs.rs#441)    where
[442](https://docs.rs#442)        Self: Sized,
[443](https://docs.rs#443)    {
[444](https://docs.rs#444)        Self::coefficient()
[445](https://docs.rs#445)    }
[446](https://docs.rs#446)}
[447](https://docs.rs#447)
[448](https://docs.rs#448)/// Trait representing a [conversion factor][factor].
[449](https://docs.rs#449)///
[450](https://docs.rs#450)/// ## Generic Parameters
[451](https://docs.rs#451)/// * `V`: Underlying storage type trait is implemented for.
[452](https://docs.rs#452)///
[453](https://docs.rs#453)/// [factor]: https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.24.html
[454](https://docs.rs#454)#[allow(unused_qualifications)] // lib:cmp::PartialOrder false positive.
[455](https://docs.rs#455)pub trait ConversionFactor<V>:
[456](https://docs.rs#456)    lib::cmp::PartialOrd
[457](https://docs.rs#457)    + lib::ops::Add<Self, Output = Self>
[458](https://docs.rs#458)    + lib::ops::Sub<Self, Output = Self>
[459](https://docs.rs#459)    + lib::ops::Mul<Self, Output = Self>
[460](https://docs.rs#460)    + lib::ops::Div<Self, Output = Self>
[461](https://docs.rs#461)    + crate::num::Zero
[462](https://docs.rs#462)    + crate::num::One
[463](https://docs.rs#463){
[464](https://docs.rs#464)    /// Raises a `ConversionFactor<V>` to an integer power.
[465](https://docs.rs#465)    #[must_use = "method returns a new number and does not mutate the original value"]
[466](https://docs.rs#466)    fn powi(self, e: i32) -> Self;
[467](https://docs.rs#467)
[468](https://docs.rs#468)    /// Converts a `ConversionFactor<V>` into its underlying storage type.
[469](https://docs.rs#469)    #[must_use = "method returns a new number and does not mutate the original value"]
[470](https://docs.rs#470)    fn value(self) -> V;
[471](https://docs.rs#471)}

[666](https://docs.rs#666)            }

[672](https://docs.rs#672)            // same number.

[713](https://docs.rs#713)    pub enum ParseQuantityError {
[714](https://docs.rs#714)        /// No separators (spaces) were encountered.
[715](https://docs.rs#715)        NoSeparator,
[716](https://docs.rs#716)

[718](https://docs.rs#718)        ///
[719](https://docs.rs#719)        /// Due to exhaustiveness and type system limitations, this variant does not encode
[720](https://docs.rs#720)        /// the underlying parse error.
[721](https://docs.rs#721)        ValueParseError,
[722](https://docs.rs#722)
[723](https://docs.rs#723)        /// The unit used wasn't found for this quantity.
[724](https://docs.rs#724)        ///
[725](https://docs.rs#725)        /// ### Notes
[726](https://docs.rs#726)        /// For now, only abbreviations are supported, so this error may be encountered even if the

[728](https://docs.rs#728)        UnknownUnit,
[729](https://docs.rs#729)    }
[730](https://docs.rs#730)
[731](https://docs.rs#731)    impl Display for ParseQuantityError {
[732](https://docs.rs#732)        fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[733](https://docs.rs#733)            use ParseQuantityError::{NoSeparator, UnknownUnit, ValueParseError};
[734](https://docs.rs#734)
[735](https://docs.rs#735)            match *self {
[736](https://docs.rs#736)                NoSeparator => write!(f, "no space between quantity and units"),
[737](https://docs.rs#737)                ValueParseError => write!(f, "error parsing unit quantity"),
[738](https://docs.rs#738)                UnknownUnit => write!(f, "unrecognized unit of measure"),
[739](https://docs.rs#739)            }
[740](https://docs.rs#740)        }
[741](https://docs.rs#741)    }

# uom::marker - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uom/0.38.0/uom/marker/index.html

## Expand description

Primitive traits and types representing basic properties of types.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Add](https://docs.rs/trait.Add.html)
- Trait to denote that a quantity is able to be added with a quantity of the same dimensions.
When a specific quantity’s kind inherits this trait `ops::Add`is implemented automatically.
- [AddAssign](https://docs.rs/trait.AddAssign.html)
- Trait to denote that a quantity is able to be added with a quantity of the same dimensions.
When a specific quantity’s kind inherits this trait `ops::AddAssign`is implemented automatically.
- [Div](https://docs.rs/trait.Div.html)
- Trait to denote that a quantity is able to be divided with a quantity of the same
dimensions. When a specific quantity’s kind inherits this trait `ops::Div`is implemented automatically.
- [DivAssign](https://docs.rs/trait.DivAssign.html)
- Trait to denote that a quantity is able to be divided with a quantity of the same
dimensions. When a specific quantity’s kind inherits this trait `ops::DivAssign`is implemented automatically.
- [Mul](https://docs.rs/trait.Mul.html)
- Trait to denote that a quantity is able to be multiplied with a quantity of the same
dimensions. When a specific quantity’s kind inherits this trait `ops::Mul`is implemented automatically.
- [MulAssign](https://docs.rs/trait.MulAssign.html)
- Trait to denote that a quantity is able to be multiplied with a quantity of the same
dimensions. When a specific quantity’s kind inherits this trait `ops::MulAssign`is implemented automatically.
- [Neg](https://docs.rs/trait.Neg.html)
- Trait to denote that a quantity is able to be negated. When a specific quantity’s kind
inherits this trait `ops::Neg`is implemented automatically.
- [Rem](https://docs.rs/trait.Rem.html)
- Trait to denote that a quantity is able to calculate a remainder with a quantity of the
same dimensions. When a specific quantity’s kind inherits this trait `ops::Rem`is implemented automatically.
- [RemAssign](https://docs.rs/trait.RemAssign.html)
- Trait to denote that a quantity is able to calculate a remainder with a quantity of the
same dimensions. When a specific quantity’s kind inherits this trait `ops::RemAssign`is implemented automatically.
- [Saturating](https://docs.rs/trait.Saturating.html)
- Trait to denote that a quantity is able to perform saturating additions and subtractions
with a quantity of the same dimensions. When a specific quantity’s kind inherits this trait
`ops::Saturating`is implemented automatically.
- [Sub](https://docs.rs/trait.Sub.html)
- Trait to denote that a quantity is able to be subtracted with a quantity of the same
dimensions. When a specific quantity’s kind inherits this trait `ops::Sub`is implemented automatically.
- [SubAssign](https://docs.rs/trait.SubAssign.html)
- Trait to denote that a quantity is able to be subtracted with a quantity of the same
dimensions. When a specific quantity’s kind inherits this trait `ops::SubAssign`is implemented automatically.

- [Unit](https://docs.rs/trait.Unit.html)

- [Units](https://docs.rs/trait.Units.html)
- Marker trait to identify a [system of units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.13.html)based on a set of[base units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.10.html)of a[system of quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.3.html).

# ISQ in uom - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uom/0.38.0/uom/macro.ISQ.html

```
macro_rules! ISQ {
    ($path:path) => { ... };
    ($path:path, $V:ty) => { ... };
    ($path:path, $V:ty, $U:tt) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Macro to implement [ Quantity](https://docs.rs/si/struct.Quantity.html) type aliases for a specific

[system of units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.13.html)and value storage type.

- `$system`: Path to the module where the- `system!`- `uom::si`).
- `$V`: Underlying value storage type (e.g.- `f32`).
- `$U`: Optional. Base units. Pass as a tuple with the desired units: (e.g.- `(meter, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, candela)`). The system’s base units will be used if no value is provided. When a value is provided a new trait type alias,- `Units`, is defined. Note that a unit with a non-zero constant factor is not currently supported as a base unit.

An example invocation is given below for a meter-kilogram-second system setup in the
module `mks` with a system of quantities name `Q`. The `#[macro_use]` attribute must be
used when including the `uom` crate to make macros for predefined systems available.
The optional units parameter to change the base units is included commented out.

```
#[macro_use]
extern crate uom;
mod f32 {
    Q!(crate::mks, f32/*, (centimeter, gram, second)*/);
}
```

# Quantity in uom::si - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uom/0.38.0/uom/si/struct.Quantity.html

```
#[repr(transparent)]pub struct Quantity<D, U, V>{
    pub dimension:
```
[PhantomData](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/struct.PhantomData.html)<D>,
    pub units: [PhantomData](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/struct.PhantomData.html)<U>,
    pub value: V,
}## Expand description

Property of a phenomenon, body or substance, where the property has a magnitude that can be expressed as a number and a reference.

The preferred method of creating a `Quantity` instance is to use the `new` constructor
which is generic over the input unit and accepts the input value as it’s only
parameter.

```
// Create a length of 1 meter.
let l = Length::new::<meter>(1.0);
```
`Quantity` fields are public to allow for the creation of `const` values and instances
of non-named `Quantity`s. This functionality will be deprecated and subsequently removed
once the [ const fn](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/24111) feature is
stabilized.

```
// Create a `const` length of 1 meter.
const L: Length = Length { dimension: PhantomData, units: PhantomData, value: 1.0, };
// Create a `const` area of 1 square meter explicitly without using the `Area` alias.
const A: Quantity<ISQ<P2, Z0, Z0, Z0, Z0, Z0, Z0>, SI<f32>, f32> =
   Quantity { dimension: PhantomData, units: PhantomData, value: 1.0, };
```
Using units for the wrong quantity will cause a compile error:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// error[E0277]: the trait bound `second: length::Unit` is not satisfied
let l = Length::new::<second>(1.0);
```
Mixing quantities will also cause a compile error:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// error[E0308]: mismatched types
let v: Velocity = Length::new::<meter>(1.0) * Time::new::<second>(1.0);
```

#### pub fn [format_args](https://docs.rs#method.format_args)<N>(_unit: N, style: [DisplayStyle](https://docs.rs/fmt/enum.DisplayStyle.html)) -> [Arguments](https://docs.rs/fmt/struct.Arguments.html)<[Dimension](https://docs.rs/absement/type.Dimension.html), N>

Creates a struct that can be used to format a compatible quantity for display.

[§](https://docs.rs#notes)Notes

The return value of this method cannot be used to print directly, but is instead
used to format quantities and can be reused; see
[ Arguments::with](https://docs.rs/fmt/struct.Arguments.html#method.with) and the examples below.

If you do not need to format multiple quantities, consider using
[ into_format_args](https://docs.rs#method.into_format_args) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
let t1 = Time::new::<femtosecond>(1.0_E-1);
let t2 = Time::new::<picosecond>(1.0_E-1);
let a = Time::format_args(femtosecond, Description);
assert_eq!("0.1 femtoseconds", format!("{}", a.with(t1)));
assert_eq!("100 femtoseconds", format!("{}", a.with(t2)));
```

Creates a struct that can be used to format a compatible quantity for display.

[§](https://docs.rs#notes-16)Notes

The return value of this method cannot be used to print directly, but is instead
used to format quantities and can be reused; see
[ Arguments::with](https://docs.rs/fmt/struct.Arguments.html#method.with) and the examples below.

If you do not need to format multiple quantities, consider using
[ into_format_args](https://docs.rs#method.into_format_args) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#notes-39)Notes

Unlike [ format_args](https://docs.rs#method.format_args), the return value of this method can be

[ format_args](https://docs.rs#method.format_args) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#notes-50)Notes

The return value of this method cannot be used to print directly, but is instead
used to format quantities and can be reused; see
[ Arguments::with](https://docs.rs/fmt/struct.Arguments.html#method.with) and the examples below.

If you do not need to format multiple quantities, consider using
[ into_format_args](https://docs.rs#method.into_format_args) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-50)Examples

```
let t1 = Time::new::<femtosecond>(1.0_E-1);

#### pub fn [format_args](https://docs.rs#method.format_args-31)<N>(_unit: N, style: [DisplayStyle](https://docs.rs/fmt/enum.DisplayStyle.html)) -> [Arguments](https://docs.rs/fmt/struct.Arguments.html)<[Dimension](https://docs.rs/electric_displacement_field/type.Dimension.html), N>

Creates a struct that can be used to format a compatible quantity for display.

[§](https://docs.rs#notes-62)Notes

The return value of this method cannot be used to print directly, but is instead
used to format quantities and can be reused; see
[ Arguments::with](https://docs.rs/fmt/struct.Arguments.html#method.with) and the examples below.

If you do not need to format multiple quantities, consider using
[ into_format_args](https://docs.rs#method.into_format_args) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-62)Examples

```
let t1 = Time::new::<femtosecond>(1.0_E-1);
let t2 = Time::new::<picosecond>(1.0_E-1);
let a = Time::format_args(femtosecond, Description);
assert_eq!("0.1 femtoseconds", format!("{}", a.with(t1)));
assert_eq!("100 femtoseconds", format!("{}", a.with(t2)));
```

Creates a struct that can be used to format a compatible quantity for display.

[§](https://docs.rs#notes-130)Notes

The return value of this method cannot be used to print directly, but is instead
used to format quantities and can be reused; see
[ Arguments::with](https://docs.rs/fmt/struct.Arguments.html#method.with) and the examples below.

If you do not need to format multiple quantities, consider using
[ into_format_args](https://docs.rs#method.into_format_args) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-130)Examples

```
let t1 = Time::new::<femtosecond>(1.0_E-1);
let t2 = Time::new::<picosecond>(1.0_E-1);
let a = Time::format_args(femtosecond, Description);
assert_eq!("0.1 femtoseconds", format!("{}", a.with(t1)));
assert_eq!("100 femtoseconds", format!("{}", a.with(t2)));
```

#### pub fn [format_args](https://docs.rs#method.format_args-71)<N>(_unit: N, style: [DisplayStyle](https://docs.rs/fmt/enum.DisplayStyle.html)) -> [Arguments](https://docs.rs/fmt/struct.Arguments.html)<[Dimension](https://docs.rs/mass_density/type.Dimension.html), N>

Creates a struct that can be used to format a compatible quantity for display.

[§](https://docs.rs#notes-142)Notes

The return value of this method cannot be used to print directly, but is instead
used to format quantities and can be reused; see
[ Arguments::with](https://docs.rs/fmt/struct.Arguments.html#method.with) and the examples below.

If you do not need to format multiple quantities, consider using
[ into_format_args](https://docs.rs#method.into_format_args) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-142)Examples

```
let t1 = Time::new::<femtosecond>(1.0_E-1);
let t2 = Time::new::<picosecond>(1.0_E-1);
let a = Time::format_args(femtosecond, Description);
assert_eq!("0.1 femtoseconds", format!("{}", a.with(t1)));
assert_eq!("100 femtoseconds", format!("{}", a.with(t2)));
```

[§](https://docs.rs#notes-153)Notes

Unlike [ format_args](https://docs.rs#method.format_args), the return value of this method can be
used directly for display. It will format the value of

`self` for the quantity on
which it is called and nothing else.If you wish to reuse the return value to format multiple quantities, use
[ format_args](https://docs.rs#method.format_args) instead.

Creates a struct that can be used to format a compatible quantity for display.

[§](https://docs.rs#notes-176)Notes

The return value of this method cannot be used to print directly, but is instead
used to format quantities and can be reused; see
[ Arguments::with](https://docs.rs/fmt/struct.Arguments.html#method.with) and the examples below.

If you do not need to format multiple quantities, consider using
[ into_format_args](https://docs.rs#method.into_format_args) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-176)Examples

```
let t1 = Time::new::<femtosecond>(1.0_E-1);
let t2 = Time::new::<picosecond>(1.0_E-1);
let a = Time::format_args(femtosecond, Description);
assert_eq!("0.1 femtoseconds", format!("{}", a.with(t1)));
assert_eq!("100 femtoseconds", format!("{}", a.with(t2)));
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/uom/si/specific_area.rs.html#3-26)#### pub fn [format_args](https://docs.rs#method.format_args-93)<N>(_unit: N, style: [DisplayStyle](https://docs.rs/fmt/enum.DisplayStyle.html)) -> [Arguments](https://docs.rs/fmt/struct.Arguments.html)<[Dimension](https://docs.rs/specific_area/type.Dimension.html), N>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/uom/si/specific_area.rs.html#3-26)

#### pub fn [format_args](https://docs.rs#method.format_args-93)<N>(_unit: N, style: [DisplayStyle](https://docs.rs/fmt/enum.DisplayStyle.html)) -> [Arguments](https://docs.rs/fmt/struct.Arguments.html)<[Dimension](https://docs.rs/specific_area/type.Dimension.html), N>

Creates a struct that can be used to format a compatible quantity for display.

[§](https://docs.rs#notes-186)Notes

The return value of this method cannot be used to print directly, but is instead
used to format quantities and can be reused; see
[ Arguments::with](https://docs.rs/fmt/struct.Arguments.html#method.with) and the examples below.

If you do not need to format multiple quantities, consider using
[ into_format_args](https://docs.rs#method.into_format_args) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-186)Examples

```
let t1 = Time::new::<femtosecond>(1.0_E-1);
let t2 = Time::new::<picosecond>(1.0_E-1);
let a = Time::format_args(femtosecond, Description);
assert_eq!("0.1 femtoseconds", format!("{}", a.with(t1)));
assert_eq!("100 femtoseconds", format!("{}", a.with(t2)));
```

#### pub fn [into_format_args](https://docs.rs#method.into_format_args-93)<N>(
    self,
    _unit: N,
    style: [DisplayStyle](https://docs.rs/fmt/enum.DisplayStyle.html),
) -> [QuantityArguments](https://docs.rs/fmt/struct.QuantityArguments.html)<[Dimension](https://docs.rs/specific_area/type.Dimension.html), U, V, N>

Creates a struct that formats `self` for display.

[§](https://docs.rs#notes-187)Notes

Unlike [ format_args](https://docs.rs#method.format_args), the return value of this method can be
used directly for display. It will format the value of

`self` for the quantity on
which it is called and nothing else.If you wish to reuse the return value to format multiple quantities, use
[ format_args](https://docs.rs#method.format_args) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-187)Examples

```
let t = Time::new::<picosecond>(1.0_E-1);
let a = t.into_format_args(femtosecond, Description);
assert_eq!("100 femtoseconds", format!("{}", a));
```

Creates a struct that can be used to format a compatible quantity for display.

[§](https://docs.rs#notes-216)Notes

The return value of this method cannot be used to print directly, but is instead
used to format quantities and can be reused; see
[ Arguments::with](https://docs.rs/fmt/struct.Arguments.html#method.with) and the examples below.

If you do not need to format multiple quantities, consider using
[ into_format_args](https://docs.rs#method.into_format_args) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-216)Examples

```
let t1 = Time::new::<femtosecond>(1.0_E-1);
let t2 = Time::new::<picosecond>(1.0_E-1);
let a = Time::format_args(femtosecond, Description);
assert_eq!("0.1 femtoseconds", format!("{}", a.with(t1)));
assert_eq!("100 femtoseconds", format!("{}", a.with(t2)));
```

[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html),

Fused multiply-add. Computes `(self * a) + b` with only one rounding error.
This produces a more accurate result with better performance than a separate
multiplication operation followed by an add.

[§](https://docs.rs#generic-parameters-1054)Generic Parameters

- `Da`: Dimension for parameter- `a`.
- `Ua`: Base units for parameter- `a`.
- `Ub`: Base units for parameter- `b`.

[Units](https://docs.rs/trait.Units.html)<

[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)> + ?

[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html),

Fused multiply-add. Computes `(self * a) + b` with only one rounding error.
This produces a more accurate result with better performance than a separate
multiplication operation followed by an add.

[§](https://docs.rs#generic-parameters-1056)Generic Parameters

- `Da`: Dimension for parameter- `a`.
- `Ua`: Base units for parameter- `a`.
- `Ub`: Base units for parameter- `b`.

Attempt to convert the given `Time` to a `Duration`.

For possible failure modes see [ TryFromError](https://docs.rs/time/enum.TryFromError.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#notes-234)Notes

The `Duration` to `Time` conversion is tested to be accurate to within 1 nanosecond (to allow
for floating point rounding error). If greater precision is needed, consider using a different
underlying storage type or avoiding the conversion altogether.

macro_rules! prefix {
    (yotta) => { ... };
    (zetta) => { ... };
    (exa) => { ... };
    (peta) => { ... };
    (tera) => { ... };
    (giga) => { ... };
    (mega) => { ... };
    (kilo) => { ... };
    (hecto) => { ... };
    (deca) => { ... };
    (none) => { ... };
    (deci) => { ... };
    (centi) => { ... };
    (milli) => { ... };
    (micro) => { ... };
    (nano) => { ... };
    (pico) => { ... };
    (femto) => { ... };
    (atto) => { ... };
    (zepto) => { ... };
    (yocto) => { ... };

## Expand description

Macro to implement the [SI](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html) prefixes for [multiples of units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.17.html),
[submultiples of units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.18.html) and [binary multiples of units](https://www.iec.ch/si/binary.htm).

Implemented using `macro_rules!` instead of `const` so that type inference at call sites can
generate the appropriate float type. Using explicit constants would require duplicate
definitions for `f32` and `f64` or casting from `f64` in `f32` contexts.

# quantity in uom - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uom/0.38.0/uom/macro.quantity.html

```
macro_rules! quantity {
    (
        $(#[$quantity_attr:meta])* quantity: $quantity:ident; $description:expr;
        $(#[$dim_attr:meta])* dimension: $system:ident<$($dimension:ident),+>;
        $(kind: $kind:ty;)?
        units {
            $($(#[$unit_attr:meta])* @$unit:ident: $coefficient:expr $(, $constant:expr)?;
                $abbreviation:expr, $singular:expr, $plural:expr;)+
        }
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Macro to implement a [quantity](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.1.html) and associated [measurement units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.9.html). Note
that this macro must be executed in direct submodules of the module where the [ system!](https://docs.rs/macro.system.html) macro
was executed.

- `$quantity_attr`: Quantity attributes. Generally used to set documentation comments for the quantity.
- `$quantity`: Quantity name (e.g.- `Length`).
- `$description`: Quantity description (e.g.- `"length"`).
- `$dim_attr`: Dimension attributes. Generally used to set documentation comments for the quantity’s dimension type alias.
- `$system`: System of quantities type (e.g.- `ISQ`).
- `$dimension`: Power of a factor for each base quantity in the system. Power should be represented as a- `typenum`type-level integer (e.g.- `N1`,- `Z0`,- `P1`,- `P2`, …).
- `$kind`:- [Kind](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.2.html)of the quantity. Optional. This variable should only be specified when defining a quantity that has the same dimensions as another quantity but isn’t comparable. When not specified- `crate::Kind`
- `$unit`: Unit name (e.g.- `meter`,- `foot`).
- `$coefficient`: Conversion coefficient from the unit to the base unit of the quantity (e.g.- `3.048_E-1`to convert- `foot`to- `meter`,- `1.0_E0`to convert- `celsius`to- `kelvin`).
- `$constant`: Optional conversion constant factor from the unit to the base unit of the quantity (e.g.- `273.15_E0`to convert- `celsius`to- `kelvin`). Note that using a unit with a non-zero constant factor is not currently supported as a base unit.
- `$abbreviation`: Unit abbreviation (e.g.- `"m"`).
- `$singular`: Singular unit description (e.g.- `"meter"`).
- `$plural`: Plural unit description (e.g.- `"meters"`).

An example invocation is given below for the quantity of length in a meter-kilogram-second
system. The `#[macro_use]` attribute must be used when including the `uom` crate to make the
`quantity!` macro available.

```
#[macro_use]
extern crate uom;
#[macro_use]
mod length {
    quantity! {
        /// Length (base unit meter, m).
        quantity: Length; "length";
        /// Length dimension, m.
        dimension: Q<P1 /*length*/, Z0 /*mass*/, Z0 /*time*/>;
        units {
            @meter: 1.0E0; "m", "meter", "meters";
            @foot: 3.048E-1; "ft", "foot", "feet";
        }
    }
}
```

---

# system in uom - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uom/0.38.0/uom/macro.system.html

```
macro_rules! system {
    (
        $(#[$quantities_attr:meta])* quantities: $quantities:ident {
            $($(#[$name_attr:meta])* $name:ident: $unit:ident, $symbol:ident;)+
        }
        $(#[$units_attr:meta])* units: $units:ident {
            $($module:ident::$quantity:ident,)+
        }
    ) => { ... };
    (
        $(#[$quantities_attr:meta])* quantities: $quantities:ident {
            $($(#[$name_attr:meta])* $name:ident: $unit:ident, $symbol:ident;)+
        }
        $(#[$units_attr:meta])* units: $units:ident {
            $(mod $module:ident::$quantity:ident,)+
        }
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Macro to implement a [system of quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.3.html).

- `$quantities_attr`: System of quantities attributes. Generally used to set documentation comments for the system of quantities.
- `$quantities`: Name of the system of quantities (e.g.- `ISQ`).
- `$name_attr`: Base quantity attributes. Generally used to set documentation comments for base units.
- `$name`: Name of the base quantities for the system of quantities (e.g.- `length`,- `mass`, …). Note that this name must match the module name of the quantity.
- `$unit`: Base unit of the quantity (e.g.- `meter`,- `kilogram`).
- `$symbol`: Dimension symbol of the quantity.
- `$units_attr`: System of units attributes. Generally used to set documentation comments for the system of units.
- `$units`: Name of the system of units (e.g.- `SI`).
- `$module`: Module name of the quantity. When prefixed by the- `mod`keyword the module must already be defined with the- `#[macro_use]`attribute. A- `#[macro_use] pub mod $module;`statement is generated if this variable is not prefixed by the- `mod`keyword.
- `$quantity`: Quantity name (e.g.- `Length`,- `Mass`, …).

An example invocation is given below for a meter-kilogram-second system. The `#[macro_use]`
attribute must be used when including the `uom` crate to make the `system!` macro available.

```
#[macro_use]
extern crate uom;
system! {
    /// System of quantities, Q.
    quantities: Q {
        length: meter, L;
        mass: kilogram, M;
        time: second, T;
    }
    /// System of units, U.
    units: U {
        mod length::Length,
        mod mass::Mass,
        mod time::Time,
    }
}
```

---

# storage_types in uom - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uom/0.38.0/uom/macro.storage_types.html

```
macro_rules! storage_types {
    ($(#[$attr:meta])* $vis:vis types: $($T:ident),+; $($tt:tt)*) => { ... };
    ($($tt:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Macro to duplicate code on a per-storage type basis. The given code is duplicated in new
modules named for each storage type. A type alias, `V`, is generated that code can use for the
type.

- `$attr`: Module attributes. Generally used to set documentation comments for storage type modules generated by the macro.
- `$T`: Types to generate a module for. Accepts all underlying storage types along with a number of different categories:- `All`:- `usize`,- `u8`,- `u16`,- `u32`,- `u64`,- `u128`,- `isize`,- `i8`,- `i16`,- `i32`,- `i64`,- `i128`,- `BigInt`,- `BigUint`,- `Rational`,- `Rational32`,- `Rational64`,- `BigRational`,- `Complex32`,- `Complex64`,- `f32`, and- `f64`.
- `PrimInt`:- `usize`,- `u8`,- `u16`,- `u32`,- `u64`,- `u128`,- `isize`,- `i8`,- `i16`,- `i32`,- `i64`, and- `i128`.
- `Ratio`:- `Rational`,- `Rational32`,- `Rational64`, and- `BigRational`.
- `Float`:- `f32`and- `f64`.
- `Signed`:- `isize`,- `i8`,- `i16`,- `i32`,- `i64`,- `i128`,- `BigInt`,- `Rational`,- `Rational32`,- `Rational64`,- `BigRational`,- `f32`, and- `f64`.
- `Unsigned`:- `usize`,- `u8`,- `u16`,- `u32`,- `u64`,- `u128`, and- `BigUint`.
- `Complex`:- `Complex32`and- `Complex64`.

- `$tt`: Code to place into each storage type module.

```
#[macro_use]
extern crate uom;
fn main() {
   f32::do_work(1.234_f32);
   f64::do_work(1.234_f64);
}
storage_types! {
   /// Type modules.
   pub types: Float;
   pub fn do_work(_v: V) {}
}
```

---

# unit in uom - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uom/0.38.0/uom/macro.unit.html

```
macro_rules! unit {
    (
        system: $system:path;
        quantity: $quantity:path;
        $($(#[$unit_attr:meta])* @$unit:ident: $coefficient:expr $(, $constant:expr)?;
            $abbreviation:expr, $singular:expr, $plural:expr;)+
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Macro to implement a set of [measurement units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.9.html). Note that units manually defined
using this macro will not be included in the quantity unit enum or associated functions, or in
the `FromStr` implementation. Using this macro will create submodules for the underlying storage
types that are enabled (e.g. `mod f32`).

When using the pre-built [SI](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html) system included with `uom` this macro allows for new units to
quickly be defined without requiring a release. [Pull requests](https://github.com/iliekturtles/uom/pulls) to add new units upstream
area always greatly appreciated.

- `$system`: Path to the module where the- `system!`- `uom::si`).
- `quantity`: Path to the module where the- `quantity!`- `uom::si::length`).
- `$unit`: Unit name (e.g.- `meter`,- `foot`).
- `$coefficient`: Conversion coefficient from the unit to the base unit of the quantity (e.g.- `3.048_E-1`to convert- `foot`to- `meter`,- `1.0_E0`to convert- `celsius`to- `kelvin`).
- `$constant`: Optional conversion constant factor from the unit to the base unit of the quantity (e.g.- `273.15_E0`to convert- `celsius`to- `kelvin`). Note that using a unit with a non-zero constant factor is not currently supported as a base unit.
- `$abbreviation`: Unit abbreviation (e.g.- `"m"`).
- `$singular`: Singular unit description (e.g.- `"meter"`).
- `$plural`: Plural unit description (e.g.- `"meters"`).

An example invocation is given below to add kilometers to length in a meter-kilogram-second
system. The `#[macro_use]` attribute must be used when including the `uom` crate to make the
`unit!` macro available.

```
#[macro_use]
extern crate uom;
unit! {
    system: crate::mks;
    quantity: crate::mks::length;
    @kilometer: 1.0E-03; "km", "kilometer", "kilometers";
}
```

---

# ConstantOp in uom - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uom/0.38.0/uom/enum.ConstantOp.html

```
pub enum ConstantOp {
    Add,
    Sub,
}
```
## Expand description

Operations performed on the constant portion of the [conversion factor](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.24.html). Used to help
guide optimizations when floating point underlying storage types are used.

For a value, `v: Float`, adding `-0.0` is a no-op while adding `0.0` will change the sign if
`v` is `-0.0`. The opposite is true for subtraction.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Add)

### Add

Hint that the constant is being added to a value.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Sub)

### Sub

Hint that the constant is being subtracted from a value.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/uom/lib.rs.html#418-420)

#### fn [coefficient](https://docs.rs#method.coefficient)() -> Self::[T](https://docs.rs/trait.Conversion.html#associatedtype.T)

Coefficient portion of [conversion factor](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.24.html) for
converting the given unit. To convert to the base unit for the quantity use `(value + constant()) * coefficient()`. To convert from the base unit, `(value / coefficient()) - constant()` is used. Implementation should return the multiplicative identity
(`Self::T::one()`) if no coefficient exists.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/uom/lib.rs.html#431-433)#### fn [constant](https://docs.rs#method.constant)(op: [ConstantOp](https://docs.rs/enum.ConstantOp.html)) -> Self::[T](https://docs.rs/trait.Conversion.html#associatedtype.T)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/uom/lib.rs.html#431-433)

#### fn [constant](https://docs.rs#method.constant)(op: [ConstantOp](https://docs.rs/enum.ConstantOp.html)) -> Self::[T](https://docs.rs/trait.Conversion.html#associatedtype.T)

Constant portion of [conversion factor](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.24.html) for
converting the given unit. To convert to the base unit for the quantity use `(value + constant()) * coefficient()`. To convert from the base unit, `(value / coefficient()) - constant()` is used. Implementation should return the additive identity (`Self::T::zero()`)
if no constant exists. See [ ConstantOp](https://docs.rs/enum.ConstantOp.html) documentation for details about parameter use to
ensure the method optimizes correctly.

# uom - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uom/latest/uom/

## Expand description

Units of measurement is a crate that does automatic type-safe zero-cost
[dimensional analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimensional_analysis). You can create your own systems or use the pre-built
[International System of Units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html) (SI) which is based on the
[International System of Quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.6.html) (ISQ) and includes numerous [quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.1.html)
(length, mass, time, …) with conversion factors for even more numerous
[measurement units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.9.html) (meter, kilometer, foot, mile, …). No more crashing your
[climate orbiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_Climate_Orbiter)!

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

`uom` requires `rustc` 1.68.0 or later. Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies]
uom = "0.38.0"
```
and this to your crate root:

`extern crate uom;`The simple example below shows how to use quantities and units as well as how `uom` stops
invalid operations:

```
extern crate uom;
use uom::si::f32::*;
use uom::si::length::kilometer;
use uom::si::time::second;
fn main() {
   let length = Length::new::<kilometer>(5.0);
   let time = Time::new::<second>(15.0);
   let velocity/*: Velocity*/ = length / time;
   let _acceleration = calc_acceleration(velocity, time);
   //let error = length + time; // error[E0308]: mismatched types
   // Get a quantity value in a specific unit.
   let time_in_nano_seconds = time.get::<uom::si::time::nanosecond>();
}
fn calc_acceleration(velocity: Velocity, time: Time) -> Acceleration {
   velocity / time
}
```
See examples provided with the source for more advanced usage including how to create `Quantity`
type aliases for a different set of base units and how to create an entirely new system of
quantities.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

`uom` has multiple `Cargo` features for controlling available underlying storage types, the
inclusion of the pre-built [International System of Units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html) (SI), support for
[Serde](https://serde.rs/), and `no_std` functionality. The features are described below. `f32`, `f64`,
`std`, and `si` are enabled by default. Features can be cherry-picked by using the
`--no-default-features` and `--features "..."` flags when compiling `uom` or specifying
features in Cargo.toml:

```
[dependencies]
uom = {
    version = "0.38.0",
    default-features = false,
    features = [
        "autoconvert", # automatic base unit conversion.
        "usize", "u8", "u16", "u32", "u64", "u128", # Unsigned integer storage types.
        "isize", "i8", "i16", "i32", "i64", "i128", # Signed integer storage types.
        "bigint", "biguint", # Arbitrary width integer storage types.
        "rational", "rational32", "rational64", "bigrational", # Integer ratio storage types.
        "complex32", "complex64", # Complex floating point storage types.
        "f32", "f64", # Floating point storage types.
        "si", "std", # Built-in SI system and std library support.
        "serde", # Serde support.
    ]
}
```
- `autoconvert`– Feature to enable automatic conversion between base units in binary operators. Disabling the feature only allows for quantities with the same base units to directly interact. The feature exists to account for compiler limitations where zero-cost code is not generated for non-floating point underlying storage types.
- `usize`,- `u8`,- `u16`,- `u32`,- `u64`,- `u128`,- `isize`,- `i8`,- `i16`,- `i32`,- `i64`,- `i128`,- `bigint`,- `biguint`,- `rational`,- `rational32`,- `rational64`,- `bigrational`,- `complex32`,- `complex64`,- `f32`,- `f64`– Features to enable underlying storage types. At least one of these features must be enabled.- `f32`and- `f64`are enabled by default. See the- [Design](https://docs.rs#design)section for implications of choosing different underlying storage types.
- `si`– Feature to include the pre-built- [International System of Units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html)(SI). Enabled by default.
- `std`– Feature to compile with standard library support. Disabling this feature compiles- `uom`with- `no_std`. Enabled by default.
- `serde`– Feature to enable support for serialization and deserialization of quantities with the- [Serde](https://serde.rs/)crate. Disabled by default.

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

Rather than working with [measurement units](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.9.html) (meter,
kilometer, foot, mile, …) `uom` works with [quantities](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.1.html)
(length, mass, time, …). This simplifies usage because units are only involved at interface
boundaries: the rest of your code only needs to be concerned about the quantities involved.
This also makes operations on quantities (+, -, *, /, …) have zero runtime cost over using
the raw storage type (e.g. `f32`).

`uom` normalizes values to the [base unit](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.10.html) for the
quantity. Alternative base units can be used by executing the macro defined for the system of
quantities (`ISQ!` for the SI). `uom` supports `usize`, `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `u128`,
`isize`, `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `i128`, `bigint`, `biguint`, `rational`, `rational32`,
`rational64`, `bigrational`, `complex32`, `complex64`, `f32`, and `f64` as the underlying
storage type.

A consequence of normalizing values to the base unit is that some values may not be able to be
represented or can’t be precisely represented for floating point and rational underlying
storage types. For example if the base unit of `length` is `meter` and the underlying storage
type is `i32` then values like `1 centimeter` or `1.1 meter` cannot be represented. `1 centimeter` is normalized to `0.01 meter` which can’t be stored in an `i32`. `uom` only allows
units to be used safely. Users of this library will still need to be aware of implementation
details of the underlying storage type including limits and precision.

[§](https://docs.rs#contributing)Contributing

Contributions are welcome from everyone. Submit a pull request, an issue, or just add comments
to an existing item. The [International Bureau of Weights and Measures](https://www.bipm.org/en/about-us/) is an
international standards organization that publishes the [SI Brochure](https://www.bipm.org/en/publications/si-brochure/). This document
defines the [SI](https://jcgm.bipm.org/vim/en/1.16.html) and can be used as a comprehensive reference for changes to `uom`. Conversion
factors for non-SI units can be found in NIST [Special Publication 811](https://www.nist.gov/pml/special-publication-811/nist-guide-si-appendix-b-conversion-factors/nist-guide-si-appendix-b9).

# Typenum

Typenum is a Rust library for type-level numbers evaluated at compile time. It currently supports bits, unsigned integers, and signed integers.

Typenum depends only on libcore, and so is suitable for use on any platform!

For the full documentation, go [here](https://docs.rs/typenum).

### Importing

While `typenum` is divided into several modules, they are all re-exported
through the crate root, so you can import anything contained herein with `use typenum::whatever;`, ignoring the crate structure.

You may also find it useful to treat the `consts` module as a prelude,
performing a glob import.

### Example

Here is a trivial example of `typenum`'s use:

```
use ;
type X = ;
assert_eq!;
type Y = ;
assert_eq!;
```
For a non-trivial example of its use, see one of the crates that depends on
it. The full list is
[here](https://crates.io/crates/typenum/reverse_dependencies). Of note are
[dimensioned](https://crates.io/crates/dimensioned/) which does compile-time
type checking for arbitrary unit systems and
[generic-array](https://crates.io/crates/generic-array/) which provides arrays
whose length you can generically refer to.

### Error messages

Typenum's error messages aren't great, and can be difficult to parse. The good
news is that the fine folks at Auxon have written a tool to help with it. Please
take a look at [tnfilt](https://github.com/auxoncorp/tnfilt).

# quickcheck 1.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/quickcheck/^1.0

# quickcheck

QuickCheck is a way to do property based testing using randomly generated input. This crate comes with the ability to randomly generate and shrink integers, floats, tuples, booleans, lists, strings, options and results. All QuickCheck needs is a property function—it will then randomly generate inputs to that function and call the property for each set of inputs. If the property fails (whether by a runtime error like index out-of-bounds or by not satisfying your property), the inputs are "shrunk" to find a smaller counter-example.

The shrinking strategies for lists and numbers use a binary search to cover
the input space quickly. (It should be the same strategy used in
[Koen Claessen's QuickCheck for
Haskell](https://hackage.haskell.org/package/QuickCheck).)

Dual-licensed under MIT or the [UNLICENSE](https://unlicense.org/).

## Documentation

The API is fully documented:
[https://docs.rs/quickcheck](https://docs.rs/quickcheck).

old versions of Rust.

Crate features:

- `"regex"`: (Enabled by default.) Enables the use of regexes with- `env_logger`.

## Minimum Rust version policy

This crate's minimum supported `rustc` version is `1.85.0`.

The current policy is that the minimum Rust version required to use this crate
can be increased in minor version updates. For example, if `crate 1.0` requires
Rust 1.20.0, then `crate 1.0.z` for all values of `z` will also require Rust
1.20.0 or newer. However, `crate 1.y` for `y > 0` may require a newer minimum
version of Rust.

In general, this crate will be conservative with respect to the minimum supported version of Rust.

With all of that said, currently, `rand` is a public dependency of
`quickcheck`. Therefore, the MSRV policy above only applies when it is more
aggressive than `rand`'s MSRV policy. Otherwise, `quickcheck` will defer to
`rand`'s MSRV policy.

## Compatibility

In general, this crate considers the `Arbitrary` implementations provided as
implementation details. Strategies may or may not change over time, which may
cause new test failures, presumably due to the discovery of new bugs due to a
new kind of witness being generated. These sorts of changes may happen in
semver compatible releases.
